title.narrative: Provision of Climate Smart WASH Services to the disaster affected children and families in Shan and Magway

description.narrative: UNICEF, in collaboration with partners, will address the immediate humanitarian needs and strengthening climate-smart Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services to 16,000 people impacted by ongoing conflict, natural disasters and climate change in Shan and Magway. In these areas, the recurrent water shortages, deterioration of WASH services due to lack of investment, damage to the WASH infrastructure and temporary displacement (or threat) due to the ongoing conflict have intensified vulnerabilities, leaving communities in immediate need of lifesaving support. Alongside water supply, sanitation, and hygiene services that address the urgent lifesaving needs, mitigating the risk of waterborne diseases and support public health, the project ensures that communities are better prepared to cope with future climate-related shocks and stress through capacity development. They will be trained to construct and maintain facilities. They will also be equipped to lead the planning, implementing and managing the interventions, thereby fostering community resilience. Building community resilience is integral to addressing humanitarian needs.Targeting 20 disaster-affected communities (10 each in Shan and Magway), the project provides a comprehensive package of interventions for households, learning centers, and healthcare facilities. This includes climate-smart WASH services, sustainable water supply with solar-powered water system, improved sanitation, and hygiene promotion that directly improve urgent and daily living conditions while fostering long-term resilience. The sanitation and hygiene promotion will be driven by locally trained volunteers who will engage with communities to improve hygiene practices. Vulnerable households unable to afford climate-resilient sanitation upgrades will receive cash assistances to procure durable, climate-resilient latrine components, coupled with technical guidance for construction. For those with the means to invest, the project will mobilize resources and technical support to upgrade household sanitation facilities, furthering resilience at the household level, and all communities are empowered to maintain them into the futureThe project promotes localisation, training local entrepreneurs and manufacturers to produce climate-resilient toilet components and provide construction services. This approach not only ensures the availability of quality materials but also stimulates local economies, creating jobs and building local capacities.Key public services infrastructure such as learning centers and healthcare facilities have suffered major setbacks resulting from the ongoing conflict. In schools and healthcare facilities, the project addresses immediate needs for safe water and sanitation while promoting sustainable hygiene practices and greening initiatives. Implementing partners will engage learners and healthcare staff in hygiene awareness campaigns, integrating these efforts with broader resilience-building activities.Communities, particularly youth, women, and marginalized groups, will take the lead in planning, implementing, and managing the interventions. Tailored training programs will build local capacities to address climate risks, leveraging traditional knowledge and practices for culturally relevant and sustainable solutions.By addressing immediate humanitarian needs of conflict- and disaster-affected communities, simultaneously building community resilience, and fostering climate adaptation, this project delivers transformative, life-saving WASH services and assistances. It ensures that conflict affected vulnerable populations in Shan and Magway not only survive the ongoing humanitarian crises but emerge better prepared and more resilient in the face of future challenges.
